headline: Revolution Wind installs final turbine off Rhode Island coast
dek: All 65 turbines now stand at the 704-megawatt offshore project, which is expected to reach full commercial operation later this year.
body: The Revolution Wind offshore project has installed its 65th and final turbine, state officials said Friday, marking a major construction milestone for the wind farm south of Rhode Island.

The 704-megawatt project sits about 15 nautical miles southeast of Point Judith. Connecticut officials said the project is expected to reach full commercial operation later this year and eventually provide enough electricity for about 350,000 homes across New England.

Connecticut is contracted to receive 304 megawatts of the project’s output, while 400 megawatts will go to Rhode Island, according to the Connecticut governor’s office. The project began construction in 2023 and started delivering some power to the regional grid in March, according to the developer.

Rhode Island Gov. Dan McKee called the installation a milestone for the state and said the project would add energy supply, union jobs and grid reliability. The remaining work is commissioning and bringing the full facility into commercial operation.
location: Offshore south of Point Judith, Rhode Island
author: NorthEast News Desk
sourceName: Governor's Offices of Rhode Island and Connecticut
